metadata.title: AN AVERAGING PROCESS FOR UNIPOTENT GROUP ACTIONS AMNON YEKUTIELI
title_lines: AN AVERAGING PROCESS FOR UNIPOTENT GROUP
metadata.abstract: W e present an averaging process for sections of a torsor unde r a unipotent group. This process allows one to integrate local sections of such a torsor into a global simplicial section. The results of this paper have applica- tions to deformation quantization of algebraic varieties. 0. Introduction Let K be a ﬁeld of characteristic 0. For any natural number q let K[t0, . . . , t q] be the polynomial algebra, and let ∆ q K be the geometric q-dimensional simplex ∆ q K := Spec K[t0, . . . , t q]/ (t0 + · · ·+ tq − 1). Our main result is the following theorem. Theorem 0.1. Let G be a unipotent algebraic group over K, let X be a K-scheme, let Z be a G-torsor over X, and let Y be any X-scheme. Suppose f = (f0, . . . , f q) is a sequence of X-morphisms fi : Y → Z. Then there is an X-morphism wavG(f ) : ∆ q K × Y → Z called the weighted average, such that the operation wavG is symmetric, simplicial, functorial in the data (G, X, Y, Z ), and is the identity for q = 0. “Symmetric” means that wav G is equivariant for the action of the permutation group of {0, . . . , q } on the sequence f and the scheme ∆ q K. “Simplicial” says that as q varies wavG : Hom X (Y, Z )q+1 → HomX (∆ q K × Y, Z ) is a map of simplicial sets. “Functorial in the data ( G, X, Y, Z )” means that e.g. given a morphism h : Z → Z′ of G-torsors over X, one has h ◦ wavG(f ) = wav G(h ◦ f ), where h ◦ f is the sequence ( h ◦ f0, . . . , h ◦ fq). Theorem 0.1 is repeated, in full detail, as Theorem 1.11. Observe that when we restrict the morphism wav G(f ) to each of the vertices of ∆ q K we recover the original morphisms f0, . . . , f q. This is due to the simplicial property of wavG. Thus wav G(f ) interpolates between f0, . . . , f q. This is illustrated in Figure 1. Date: 12 January 2006.
